entities.name: Sieghard von Aquileia
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Sigehard or Sieghard, also known as Sigehard of Beilstein, was a patriarch of Aquileia from 1068 to 1077. He was a member of a Bavarian noble family with estates in Chiemgau.

Sigehard was born into a powerful family and was appointed patriarch of Aquileia at a young age. He played a significant role in the governance of the city and was known for his religious leadership.

Sigehard's legacy includes his efforts to maintain the influence of the Holy Roman Empire in the region. His successors continued to shape the religious and political landscape of Aquileia, which remained an important center of Christianity in Western Europe.

The sheer scale of his influence can be measured in the enduring legacy of the Holy Roman Empire, which continued to shape European politics and society for centuries after his death.

 Sigehard of Beilstein is a fascinating case study in the complexities of medieval power dynamics, and his impact on the region is still felt today.
